Redirect Rule Generator

301 redirect rules for Apache, Nginx, HTML and JavaScript.


      

      

      

    

    

      
    

    
HTML and JavaScript redirects are client-side fallbacks — prefer a real server 301 whenever you can.

  





  
  


  

    

      
📖 How to use

      
  1. Enter one redirect per line as: old-path -> new-url.
  2. Click Generate redirects.
  3. Switch between the Apache, Nginx, HTML and JavaScript tabs.
  4. Copy the block you need into your server config or page.

    

    

      
❓ Frequently asked questions

      
Which redirect formats are generated?
Apache .htaccess uses Redirect 301, Nginx uses rewrite … permanent, HTML uses a meta refresh tag, and JavaScript uses window.location.replace — all four are generated from the same list.
Is a 301 better than a meta refresh?
A 301 tells browsers and search engines the move is permanent, so link equity passes to the new URL. Meta refresh and JavaScript redirects are client-side fallbacks.
Are special characters escaped?
Yes — old paths are regex-escaped for Nginx and quotes are escaped for Apache, HTML and JavaScript output.
